## The hill

The SNOWFALL background has been rebuilt from nothing. It used to be
seventy white pixels falling straight down and a snowman that, it turns
out, was being drawn *behind* the detection counters the entire time.
It is now a night ski hill with a moon over it, a gondola line crossing
the sky, and a yeti who is usually not quite fast enough.

### Thanks, Houdini

Before any of the rest of it: **Houdini has been testing every
single build of this thing**, patiently, for a long time —
including the ones that boot-looped, the ones where the sky came out
green, and the deliberately absurd one where six things happened at once
just to find out where the limit was. Most of what is good in this
release is good because somebody actually ran the bad version first and
said so. Cheers, mate. This one is for you.

### Parallax that means something

Three planes, and the rule that makes them work is that **speed, size and
height all move together**. Far trees are small, sit high on a ridge
line, and crawl. The trees on the skier's own plane are full size, stand
on the snow, and move at the world's pace. A single foreground pine is
enormous, sits below the frame, and sweeps past fast.

The old version gave every tree the same height and the same ground line
but a random speed, which is exactly what read as broken — identical
objects at identical distance cannot be travelling at different rates.

**The trees are also 2.1x the skier now.** They used to be the same
height as him, which quietly made him a giant.

### Cat and mouse

The yeti chases the skier, and **most of the time the skier gets away**.
There are five ways it can end and only one of them is dinner:

- he loses interest and lopes off
- he runs out of wind, stops, and stands there with his hands on his
  knees
- he trips and goes face down in the snow with his legs still going
- the skier turns round and beats him off with a ski pole
- or, about one time in six, he catches him

The outcome is decided the moment he sets off and his speed follows from
it, so a yeti who is going to lose is visibly slower the whole way rather
than changing his mind at the last second.

**And when he does win there is a proper animation for it** — grab, then
head first and horizontal into the jaw with the skis still trailing out
sideways, then a chomp, then a swallow that visibly fills him out, then a
pat on the belly. Drawn from the original sprite rather than guessed at.

### The rest of the hill

**Jumps.** Ramps come down the slope and he hits them, launches, and
pulls either a tuck or a spread-eagle before landing.

**Tracks.** He cuts a line into the bank wherever he actually goes, and
fresh snow slowly fills it back in.

**Weather that builds.** Calm most of the time, with squalls and the
occasional whiteout, and the bank grows and melts with it.

**A moon with a real glow**, gondola cabins with lit windows, and a
**dawn** that comes round every few minutes — it warms the sky, sets the
moon, melts the snow faster, and keeps the yeti off the hill entirely.

### The bubblegum actually appears now

Squachy's gum bubble was on a squared growth curve, which is the
physically honest one — a real bubble does start slow — but it meant the
thing spent its first full second under six pixels across and only
looked like a bubble for the few frames before it burst. What you
actually saw was a pop with nothing in front of it. It reaches a
readable size in about a third of a second now and holds there before it
goes.

### The actually-useful part
- **Changed**: SNOWFALL completely rebuilt — three-plane parallax, weather, accumulation, tracks, jumps, gondolas, moon, dawn
- **Added**: the SkiFree yeti, with five different ways a chase can end and a full eating animation for the one that goes badly
- **Fixed**: everything on the hill now stands on the background's real floor instead of behind the detection counters
- **Fixed**: the gum bubble was invisible for most of its life
- **Note**: this is the heaviest background on the device. If you want the smoothest version of it, use the 80 MHz display option in the flasher
